content:
- When sentiment is negative in the recent history, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen subsequent forecast peaks.
- If sentiment is consistently positive, model tends to overestimate future prices; apply downward bias to later forecast days.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or mixed — increase forecast mid-range values.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing short-term sentiment shifts — adjust early days to align with sentiment direction.
- When sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust downward — apply downward correction starting from that point.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model tends to hold high prices longer than observed; introduce early mean-reversion decay in forecast.
